correctness.rationale: For all fixed a>b>0 and beta>0, an exact Bessel/reflection kernel yields joint unnormalized mass C_beta exp(-lambda t) rho^j i^(-beta) B_t(i,j). The Fourier sine integral gives uniform Gaussian-scaling and microscopic i,j expansions and an ij t^(-3/2) global bound; an exponentially tilted Skellam bound controls diffusive and larger i. Weighted Riemann sums prove the Gamma entrance for beta<2; harmonic sums yield the logarithmic-uniform entrance at beta=2; dominated convergence in the product counting measure proves total variation and power-law size bias for beta>2. Terminal tail control makes all three limits joint independent products with the normalized minimal-QSD law. The packaged standard-library checker passed 3622 assertions, and the optional numerical experiment was checked; neither finite test is substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Critical-geometric initial tails sit precisely at the boundary of minimal-QSD attraction. Knowing a terminal QSD or a survival exponent leaves the survivor-selected starting depth completely undetermined. The theorem finds a sharp phase transition: diffusive Gamma entrance when beta<2, an entire uniform continuum of polynomial entrance scales at beta=2, and discrete size-biasing when beta>2, always asymptotically independent of the terminal state. This gives motivated ancestral localization, not a cosmetic correction to a known survival constant.
